examples.en: The file was copied to another folder.

examples.ko: 사진이 잘못 복사돼서 두 장이 됐어요.
examples.en: The photo got copied by mistake and became two.
The content must not be copied as it is.
The email address won't copy.
Please leave the copied documents here.

examples.ko: 그 글이 인터넷에서 계속 복사되고 있어요.
examples.en: That post keeps getting copied around the internet.

explain: 복사되다는 파일이나 서류처럼 복사되는 물건이 주어일 때 써요. 복사하는 사람이 주어이면 '복사하다'를 써요. '복사돼요', '복사됐어요'처럼 '되어'가 '돼'로 줄어드는 것도 기억하세요.
explain_en: 복사되다 is used when the thing being copied, like a file or a document, is the subject. When a person does the copying, use 복사하다. Remember that 되어 shortens to 돼, as in 복사돼요 and 복사됐어요.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹고 바로 누우면 소화가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you lie down right after eating, you don't digest well.
This food is digested slowly.

examples.ko: 어제 먹은 게 아직 소화되지 않았어요.
examples.en: What I ate yesterday still hasn't digested.

examples.ko: 우유는 소화되기 어렵다고 말하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say milk is hard to digest.
Porridge is food that digests easily in the stomach.
If your food has settled, let's go for a walk.

explain: 음식이 주어이면 '소화되다', 먹는 사람이 주어이면 '소화하다'를 써요. 배가 불편할 때는 '소화가 안 돼요'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Use 소화되다 when the food is the subject and 소화하다 when the eater is the subject. When your stomach feels bad, you can say 소화가 안 돼요.

examples.en: After dinner I walked to help my food settle.
I took the stairs to help digest my food.

examples.ko: 위가 음식을 소화시키는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time for the stomach to digest food.
I'm full, so I'll let it settle before I work out.

examples.ko: 아기가 우유를 소화시키지 못해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The baby couldn't digest milk, so we went to the hospital.
I drink coffee after my lunch has settled.

explain: '소화되다'는 음식이 저절로 소화되는 것이고, '소화시키다'는 사람이나 몸이 소화되게 만드는 것이에요. 산책이나 운동처럼 일부러 하는 행동 뒤에 자연스럽게 나와요.
explain_en: 소화되다 means food gets digested on its own, while 소화시키다 means a person or body makes it digest. It fits naturally after deliberate actions like a walk or exercise.

examples.ko: 위가 음식을 소화하는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: The stomach takes time to digest food.
Yesterday was hard because I got through the whole schedule.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 키 큰 사람만 소화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only tall people can pull off this outfit.
The baby can't digest meat yet.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 어려운 역할을 잘 소화했어요.
examples.en: The actor handled the difficult role well.

examples.ko: 이 많은 숙제를 하루에 다 소화하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to get through all this homework in one day.

explain: 음식을 소화하는 것 말고도 많은 일정이나 어려운 역할, 눈에 띄는 옷을 잘 해내는 것에도 써요. 몸 이야기가 아니면 '해내다'와 비슷한 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 이번 주에는 일정을 다 소화하기 어려워요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 일이 많을 때 그 일을 끝까지 해낸다는 뜻으로 써요. 음식 이야기가 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is a lot to do and you manage to complete it all. It has nothing to do with food.

explain_en: Besides digesting food, it is also used for getting through a heavy schedule, handling a hard role, or pulling off a bold outfit. When it is not about the body, it feels close to 해내다.

examples.en: The council meeting is tomorrow afternoon.
I attended the parents' council meeting.
The council decided on new rules.
The residents set up a council themselves.
I heard the council schedule changed.
Who is the head of our neighborhood council?

explain: 협의회는 여러 사람이나 단체가 의견을 맞추려고 만든 모임에 써요. '학부모협의회'나 '시민협의회'처럼 앞에 이름이 붙는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 회의 한 번을 말할 때는 '회의'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 협의회 is used for a group that people or organizations form to coordinate their opinions. A name often comes before it, as in 학부모협의회 or 시민협의회. For a single ordinary meeting, 회의 is more natural.

examples.en: The Earth rotates once a day.
The ride started to spin slowly.
The wheel is spinning very fast.

examples.ko: 이 손잡이는 오른쪽으로 회전하면 소리가 커져요.
examples.en: If you turn this knob to the right, the volume goes up.
The fan blades spin and the air comes out.
Try going in through the revolving door.

explain: 바퀴나 지구처럼 축을 중심으로 도는 것에 써요. 사람이 몸을 돌릴 때는 '돌다'나 '돌아서다'가 자연스러워요. 차가 길에서 방향을 바꾸는 것은 '우회전', '좌회전'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for things that turn around an axis, like a wheel or the Earth. When a person turns their body, 돌다 or 돌아서다 sounds more natural. A car turning at a corner is called 우회전 or 좌회전.

examples.en: I have to submit documents to the office of education.

examples.ko: 시 교육청에서 새 소식을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The city office of education shared some news.
The education office building is next to city hall.
The office of education supports school events.
I looked up our local education office's website.
The teacher went to a training session at the education office.

explain: '교육부'는 나라 전체의 교육을 맡고, '교육청'은 시·도 단위로 학교를 관리해요. 학교 일은 학교를 거쳐 교육청에 올라가요. '서울시교육청'처럼 지역 이름을 앞에 붙여요.
explain_en: '교육부' handles education for the whole country, while a '교육청' manages the schools of a city or province. School matters go up through the school to the 교육청. The region name goes in front, as in '서울시교육청'.

examples.en: My whole family is safe.
There was an accident, but luckily I was unharmed.
I heard the news that the child is safe.
Seeing you safe puts my mind at ease.
I'm worried whether he is safe.
I hope the luggage arrives safely.

explain: 사고나 위험 뒤에 사람이 다치지 않고 괜찮을 때 써요. 장소나 상황이 위험하지 않다고 말할 때는 '안전하다'를 써요. '무사히 도착했어요'처럼 부사 '무사히'로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used for a person who came through an accident or danger without harm. To say that a place or situation is not dangerous, use 안전하다. The adverb 무사히 is also common, as in 무사히 도착했어요.

examples.en: I'm not unhappy right now.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 불행한 일을 많이 겪었어요.
examples.en: That person went through many unfortunate events.
He had an unhappy-looking face.
You can be unhappy even if you have a lot of money.
Unfortunately, it rained and the event was canceled.
She said her childhood was unhappy.

explain: 반대말은 '행복하다'예요. '불행하다'는 꽤 무거운 말이라서 오늘 기분이 안 좋을 때는 '속상해요', '우울해요'를 더 많이 써요. '불행하게도'는 나쁜 소식을 전할 때 앞에 붙이는 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is 행복하다. 불행하다 is a fairly heavy word, so for a bad mood today you would say 속상해요 or 우울해요 instead. 불행하게도 is placed in front when you deliver bad news.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 새 제품을 위해 제휴했어요.
examples.en: The two companies partnered up for a new product.

examples.ko: 카페가 은행과 제휴해서 할인을 해 줘요.
examples.en: The cafe has partnered with a bank to offer discounts.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 외국 대학과 제휴하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our school has a partnership with a foreign university.
We are looking for a company to partner with.
The app decided to partner with a movie theater.
We plan to team up with another shop.

explain: 'A와 제휴하다'처럼 조사 '와/과'와 같이 써요. 보통 회사나 기관 사이에서 서로 돕기로 약속할 때 쓰고, 친구 사이에는 쓰지 않아요. '제휴 카드', '제휴 할인'처럼 명사로 붙이는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used with the particle 와/과, as in 'A와 제휴하다'. It is usually for companies or organizations agreeing to cooperate, not for friends. It also attaches to nouns, as in 제휴 카드 and 제휴 할인.

examples.en: I got a pearl necklace as a birthday gift.
Pearls form inside shellfish.
The white glow of the pearl is beautiful.

examples.ko: 이 반지에는 작은 진주가 박혀 있어요.
examples.en: A small pearl is set in this ring.
I opened the shell and there was a pearl.
I bought pearls as a wedding present.

explain: '진주'는 경상남도에 있는 도시 이름이기도 해요. 보석은 '진주 목걸이', '진주 귀걸이'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 자주 써요.
explain_en: 진주 is also the name of a city in South Gyeongsang Province. The gem is often placed before another noun, as in 진주 목걸이 and 진주 귀걸이.

examples.en: The county governor came to the village event.
The county governor often listens to residents.
I wrote a letter to the county governor.
The county governor election is next month.
I received the documents at the county governor's office.

examples.ko: 시골 마을에서는 군수를 가까이에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: In a country village you can see the governor up close.

explain: 도시의 책임자는 '시장', 구는 '구청장', 군은 '군수'라고 해요. '군'은 도시보다 작은 시골 지역에 많아요. 높여서 '군수님'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: The head of a city is a 시장, of a district a 구청장, and of a county a 군수. A 군 is a rural area smaller than a city. To be polite you say 군수님.

examples.en: I bought clothes whose colors go well together.
The name and the photo don't match.
The shoes go well with the bag, so it looks nice.
Once the information matches, the check is done.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 조건이 매치되었다는 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a message saying their conditions matched.
A message appeared saying the data doesn't match.

explain: 영어 match에서 온 말이라서 옷 색깔이나 정보가 맞을 때 써요. 옷이 어울릴 때는 '어울리다'로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 사람이 주어가 되어 직접 맞출 때는 '매치하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It comes from English 'match' and is used when clothing colors or pieces of information fit together. For clothes that suit each other, you can swap in 어울리다. When a person does the matching, use 매치하다.

examples.en: I paired a white shirt with jeans.
It's hard to match colors.

examples.ko: 가방과 신발을 같은 색으로 매치해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried matching the bag and shoes in the same color.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 사용자와 친구를 매치해 줘요.
examples.en: This app matches users with friends.
I don't know how I should pair them.
I solved a problem about matching two lists.

explain: 'A에 B를 매치하다'처럼 옷이나 색을 맞춰 입을 때 자주 써요. 같은 상황에서 '코디하다'도 쓰고, '어울리게 입다'라고도 해요. 이름과 짝을 찾을 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is often used for coordinating an outfit or colors, as in 'A에 B를 매치하다'. In the same situation people also say 코디하다 or 어울리게 입다. It is also used for pairing names with their partners.

examples.en: I was assigned to class 3.
The room hasn't been assigned yet.
A desk was assigned to the new employee.
Homework is assigned differently to each student.
Please sit in your assigned seat.
The budget will be allotted next month.

explain: 'N에 배정되다'처럼 조사 '에'와 같이 써요. 반 배정, 좌석 배정, 예산 배정처럼 사람이나 자원을 정해진 곳에 나눠 줄 때 나와요. 나눠 주는 쪽이 주어이면 '배정하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used with the particle 에, as in 'N에 배정되다'. It appears with class assignment, seat assignment, or budget allocation, where people or resources are given to a set place. When the one who assigns is the subject, use 배정하다.

examples.en: The teacher assigned the students to classes.
I'll assign your room first.
We are dividing and assigning the work to each person.
It takes time to assign the seats.
We will allot the budget to each department.
We haven't assigned a person in charge yet.

explain: 'A를 B에 배정하다'처럼 누구를 어디에 정해 줄 때 써요. 정해 주는 사람이 주어이고, 정해진 사람이 주어이면 '배정되다'를 써요. 단순히 일을 시킬 때는 '맡기다'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: It is used in 'A를 B에 배정하다' when someone decides where someone or something goes. The person deciding is the subject; if the assigned person is the subject, use 배정되다. For simply handing someone a job, 맡기다 is easier.

examples.en: That movie will be shown next week.

examples.ko: 이 영화관에서 한국 영화가 상영되고 있어요.
examples.en: A Korean film is showing at this theater.
The movie shown today was fun.
Ads played before the film was shown.

examples.ko: 단편 영화 세 편이 상영될 거예요.
examples.en: Three short films will be screened.
That work was screened overseas too.

explain: 영화가 주어일 때 '상영되다'를 써요. 영화관에서 영화를 틀어 주는 것이 '상영하다'예요. 연극이나 콘서트는 '상영' 대신 '공연'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use 상영되다 when the movie is the subject. Showing a film in a theater is 상영하다. For plays or concerts, say 공연 instead of 상영.

examples.en: The theater is showing a new movie.
The school screened a documentary.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 오늘 몇 시에 상영하나요?
examples.en: What time does that movie show today?

examples.ko: 영화를 상영하는 동안 휴대폰을 꺼 주세요.
examples.en: Please turn off your phone while the film is playing.

examples.ko: 공원에서 매주 금요일에 영화를 상영해 줘요.
examples.en: They show a movie in the park every Friday.
They will start showing that movie tomorrow.

explain: 극장이나 행사에서 영화를 틀어 줄 때 써요. 집에서 영화를 볼 때는 '상영' 대신 '틀다'나 '보다'를 써요. 연극이나 콘서트는 '공연하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when a theater or event plays a film. At home you would say 틀다 or 보다 rather than 상영하다. For plays and concerts, use 공연하다.

examples.en: The child depends too much on his parents.

examples.ko: 저는 지도 앱에 의존해서 길을 찾아요.
examples.en: I rely on a map app to find my way.
This shop depends on tourists.
I want to live without relying on others.
I want to fix my habit of depending on my smartphone.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 에너지를 수입에 의존할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Our country has no choice but to rely on imports for energy.

explain: 사람에게는 '에게', 사물이나 나라에는 '에'를 붙여 '~에게/에 의존하다'로 써요. '의지하다'는 마음으로 기대는 따뜻한 느낌이고, '의존하다'는 지나치게 기댄다는 느낌이 들 수 있어요.
explain_en: Attach 에게 for people and 에 for things or countries: '~에게/에 의존하다'. 의지하다 has a warm feeling of leaning on someone emotionally, while 의존하다 can suggest leaning too much.

examples.en: The culprit is presumed to be a man.

examples.ko: 사고 원인은 운전자 실수로 추측되고 있어요.
examples.en: The cause of the accident is presumed to be driver error.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 백 년 전에 지어졌다고 추측되어요.
examples.en: This building is thought to have been built a hundred years ago.
The exact time can't be guessed.

examples.ko: 그렇게 추측되는 이유가 몇 가지 있어요.
examples.en: There are a few reasons why it is presumed so.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 삼백 년 전에 그려진 것으로 추측됐어요.
examples.en: This painting is presumed to have been drawn three hundred years ago.

explain: '~로 추측되다', '~것으로 추측되다'처럼 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '~인 것 같아요', '아마 ~일 거예요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It appears as '~로 추측되다' or '~것으로 추측되다', mostly in news and explanatory writing. In speech, '~인 것 같아요' or '아마 ~일 거예요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: A sponge absorbs water.
The plant took in water through its roots.

examples.ko: 우리 몸은 비타민을 장에서 흡수하고 나머지는 내보내요.
examples.en: Our body absorbs vitamins in the intestines and sends out the rest.

examples.ko: 아이들은 새로운 지식을 빠르게 흡수하는 편이에요.
examples.en: Children tend to absorb new knowledge quickly.
This fabric can't absorb sweat.

examples.ko: 큰 회사가 작은 회사를 흡수할 거예요.
examples.en: The big company will absorb the small one.

explain: 물이나 영양분이 스며드는 것뿐 아니라 지식, 문화를 받아들이는 것에도 써요. 회사가 다른 회사를 합칠 때도 '흡수하다'를 써요. 물건이 물을 빨아들이는 것은 일상에서 '빨아들이다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Besides water and nutrients soaking in, it is used for taking in knowledge or culture, and for a company merging another one into itself. In everyday talk a thing drawing in water can also be called 빨아들이다.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 취미가 공통돼서 금방 친해졌어요.
examples.en: The two quickly became close because they share hobbies.
These stories don't share a theme.
The two stories share a theme.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에 공통된 점이 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: The two have nothing in common.

examples.ko: 이 두 나라는 문화가 공통되는 부분이 많아요.
examples.en: These two countries have many parts of their culture in common.
To become friends, you need a shared topic.

explain: '비슷하다'는 모양이나 성질이 닮았다는 뜻이고, '공통되다'는 둘 이상이 함께 가진 점이 있다는 뜻이에요. '공통되는', '공통된'처럼 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태가 가장 많아요. '공통점', '공통으로'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: '비슷하다' means looking or being alike, while '공통되다' means two or more things share something. It appears most often in the noun-modifying forms '공통되는' and '공통된'. '공통점' and '공통으로' are also common.

examples.en: The winter of that year was really cold.
I came to Korea for the first time that year.
It rained a lot that year.
I still remember what happened that year.
I started writing a diary every day from that year.
That year, too, was coming to an end before I knew it.

explain: '그해'는 한 단어라서 붙여 써요. 앞에서 말한 해를 다시 가리킬 때 써서 주로 이야기 속 지난 일에 나와요. 지금 말하는 해는 '올해', 지난해는 '작년'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 그해 is one word, so it is written without a space. It points back to a year already mentioned, so it mostly appears in stories about the past. The current year is 올해 and last year is 작년.

examples.en: When a problem comes up, you have to deal with it calmly.
I learned how to deal with earthquakes.

examples.ko: 그 직원은 손님의 불만에 잘 대처했어요.
examples.en: The employee handled the customer's complaint well.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 상황에 어떻게 대처할지 생각해 봤어요.
examples.en: I thought about how to cope with a sudden situation.

examples.ko: 위기에 잘 대처하면 기회가 생길 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you handle a crisis well, an opportunity may come.
We train every month to be ready for emergencies.

explain: '문제에 대처하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 같이 써요. '를'은 쓰지 않아요. 대상은 문제, 위기, 갑작스러운 상황처럼 어려운 일이에요. 가벼운 일에는 '처리하다'가 어울려요.
explain_en: It goes with the particle 에, as in '문제에 대처하다', not 를. The target is a difficult thing like a problem, a crisis, or a sudden situation. For lighter matters, 처리하다 fits better.

examples.ko: 주민 총회가 이번 주 토요일에 열려요.
examples.en: The residents' general meeting is this Saturday.
We elected a new president at the general meeting.
I took a day off to attend the general meeting.
The club holds a general meeting at year-end.
Please read the general meeting materials in advance.
The general meeting ended in an hour.

explain: '정기 총회', '임시 총회'처럼 앞에 말이 붙는 일이 많아요. 회사에서는 '주주총회'라고 해요. 아파트나 동호회에서도 총회를 열어요.
explain_en: A modifier often comes before it, as in 정기 총회 or 임시 총회. In companies it is 주주총회. Apartment complexes and clubs also hold a 총회.

en: be cut; be chopped; be hacked

examples.en: My finger got cut on paper.
I got cut by a knife and bled.
I didn't know my leg had been cut by the grass.
Be careful not to get cut by the glass.
I cut my chin while shaving and it hurt.

examples.ko: 요리하다가 손이 베이면 먼저 물로 씻으세요.
examples.en: If your hand gets cut while cooking, rinse it with water first.

explain: 날카로운 것에 몸이 상처 날 때 '~에 베이다'라고 해요. 같은 상황에서 가시나 바늘은 '찔리다'를 써요. 칼로 일부러 자르는 것은 '베다' 쪽이라서 '베이다'와 다르게 써요.
explain_en: When something sharp wounds your body, you say '~에 베이다'. For thorns or needles, use 찔리다 instead. Cutting something on purpose with a blade is the verb 베다, which differs from 베이다.

examples.ko: 이 화장품은 피부에 먼저 바르는 베이스예요.
examples.en: This cosmetic is the base you put on your skin first.
The choir needs a low bass voice.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 한국어 학습을 베이스로 만들었어요.
examples.en: This app was built with Korean learning as its base.
The runner stepped on first base.
The base of this sauce is tomato.

examples.ko: 저는 요즘 베이스 기타를 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: These days I'm learning the bass guitar.

explain: 영어 base(바탕)와 bass(낮은 소리)가 한국어에서는 둘 다 '베이스'가 돼요. 글자는 같아서 문맥으로 구분해요. 야구에서는 '루', 음악에서는 '베이스 기타'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 달라요.
explain_en: English 'base' and 'bass' both become 베이스 in Korean, so you tell them apart by context. In baseball it goes with 루, and in music with phrases like 베이스 기타.

examples.en: My younger sibling attends an art academy.
I'm learning to cook at an academy.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 아카데미 시상식에서 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: That film won an award at the Academy Awards.
A new academy opened in our neighborhood.
Academy classes start in the evening.
My friend works as an instructor at an English academy.

explain: 한국에서는 학원 이름에 '아카데미'를 붙이는 곳이 있어요. 영화의 '아카데미상'에도 같은 말이 들어가요. 일반적인 학원을 부를 때는 '학원'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Some private institutes in Korea put 아카데미 in their names. The same word is part of the film award 아카데미상. For a typical cram school or institute, the usual word is 학원.

examples.en: The book is being printed and comes out today.
The name was printed wrong.
It takes two days for the poster to be printed.
The date is printed on the ticket.
Please check the printed document.
The file wouldn't print, so I checked the printer.

explain: 종이나 물건 위에 글자가 찍힐 때 그 글자나 책이 주어이면 '인쇄되다'를 써요. 사람이 프린터로 찍는 것은 '인쇄하다', 보통은 '프린트하다'나 '출력하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use 인쇄되다 when the text or book is the subject that gets printed on paper or an object. A person printing with a printer is 인쇄하다, and people often say 프린트하다 or 출력하다 too.

examples.en: That pitcher is our team's ace.
The sales team's ace received an award.
The coach entrusted the last game to the ace.
The star player scored at the end.
I played the ace in the card game.
The star of our class is a runner.

explain: 운동 팀뿐 아니라 직장이나 학교에서 가장 믿음직하고 뛰어난 사람에게도 써요. 카드 게임의 A 카드도 '에이스'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used not only for sports teams but also for the most dependable and outstanding person at a workplace or school. The A card in card games is also called 에이스.

examples.en: I left my charging cable behind.
The cable is short, so it doesn't reach the bed.
The cable connection is wrong.
I replaced the TV cable at home.

examples.ko: 이 케이블은 컴퓨터와 모니터를 이어 줘요.
examples.en: This cable connects the computer and the monitor.

examples.ko: 책상 뒤 케이블에 걸려서 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost tripped on a cable behind the desk.

explain: 충전 케이블, USB 케이블처럼 기기를 잇는 줄에 많이 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '선'이라고도 해요. '케이블카', '케이블 TV'처럼 다른 말과 합쳐지기도 해요.
explain_en: It is commonly used for wires that connect devices, like a charging cable or USB cable. In daily talk people also just say 선. It also joins other words, as in 케이블카 and 케이블 TV.

examples.en: A hiker went missing in the mountains yesterday.
I saw news that a child had gone missing.
I'm looking for a missing puppy.
When the ship went missing at sea, the rescue team was sent out.
He was found three days after he went missing.
If a family member goes missing, you must report it to the police.

explain: 사람이나 동물이 사라져서 있는 곳을 알 수 없을 때 써요. 물건에는 '분실되다'나 '잃어버리다'를 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 무거운 말이라서 일상에서 가볍게 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used when a person or animal has vanished and nobody knows where they are. For objects, use 분실되다 or 잃어버리다. It is a heavy word heard in the news, so it is not used lightly in daily talk.

examples.en: This monitor is 27 inches.
Some TVs are over 55 inches.
My laptop is only 15 inches.
I bought the 32-inch one because the screen is bigger.
One inch is about 2.5 centimeters.
What size tablet, in inches, do you want to buy?

explain: TV나 모니터, 휴대폰 화면 크기는 센티미터가 아니라 '인치'로 말해요. '27인치'처럼 숫자 뒤에 붙여 써도 되고 띄어 써도 돼요.
explain_en: Screen sizes of TVs, monitors, and phones are given in 인치, not centimeters. It can be written attached to the number or with a space, as in 27인치 or 27 인치.

examples.en: I got the date wrong and came early.
I mistook someone else for my friend.
I think I got something mixed up.
I set an alarm so I wouldn't mix up the time.
I mistakenly thought it was Monday and went to school.

examples.ko: 자기가 제일 잘한다고 착각하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people delude themselves into thinking they're the best.

explain: 'A를 B로 착각하다'처럼 다른 것을 같은 것으로 잘못 생각할 때 써요. '오해하다'는 상대 말이나 행동의 뜻을 잘못 받아들이는 것이라서 다르게 써요. 명사 '착각'은 '착각이에요', '착각에 빠지다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used in 'A를 B로 착각하다' when you wrongly take one thing for another. 오해하다 means misreading what someone said or did, so it is used differently. The noun 착각 appears in 착각이에요 and 착각에 빠지다.

examples.en: That athlete has great running form.
Form matters most when you work out.
My friend struck a pose for the photo.

examples.ko: 골프 폼에 문제가 있어서 고치고 있어요.
examples.en: My golf form has a problem, so I'm fixing it.
Today I went out dressed stylishly.
My condition is good lately, so my form has improved.

explain: 영어 form에서 온 말로, 운동 자세를 말할 때와 겉모습이 멋있을 때 써요. 서류의 '양식'을 뜻하는 form은 '폼'보다 '양식'이나 '서식'이라고 하는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 멋있어 보이려고 일부러 자세나 표정을 꾸밀 때 써요. 조금 놀리는 느낌이 있을 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone deliberately arranges their posture or expression to look cool. It can sound a little teasing.

explain_en: It comes from English 'form' and is used for exercise posture and for looking cool. For a document form, 양식 or 서식 is more natural than 폼.

examples.en: I practiced like it was the real thing before the exam.
In the real situation I got nervous and made a mistake.
Try solving the practice-test questions.
She is a teacher with a lot of hands-on experience.
Practice and the real thing are very different.
Real-world practice matters for driving.

explain: '연습'과 짝으로 써요. 시험이나 경기처럼 진짜 해야 하는 순간을 말해요. '실전 문제', '실전 모의고사'처럼 시험 준비 책 이름에도 자주 붙어요.
explain_en: It pairs with 연습 as its counterpart. It refers to the moment you actually have to perform, like an exam or a match. It is also attached to study-book titles such as 실전 문제 and 실전 모의고사.

examples.en: The school does not tolerate violence.
I can't tolerate that kind of lie.
The company let the small mistake slide.
My parents tolerated coming home late.

examples.ko: 이 정도 지각은 용인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A lateness this small is acceptable.
We must not tolerate false advertising.

explain: '허락하다'는 해도 된다고 말해 주는 것이고, '용인하다'는 문제인 줄 알면서도 막지 않고 받아들이는 느낌이에요. '용인하지 않아요'는 그냥 안 된다고 선을 긋는 말이에요. 같은 소리의 '용인'은 경기도의 도시 이름이기도 해요.
explain_en: 허락하다 means telling someone they may do it, while 용인하다 feels like knowing something is a problem but not stopping it. 용인하지 않아요 draws a firm line that it is not allowed. The same sound 용인 is also the name of a city in Gyeonggi Province.

examples.en: My parents run a business at the market.
I opened a shop with the money I earned from trading.
These days it's a hard time to run a business.
Since I started running a shop, the day passes really fast.
I learned how to do business from a young age.

examples.ko: 장사를 하려면 손님이 많은 곳이 좋아요.
examples.en: To run a shop, a place with many customers is good.

explain: 장사는 가게나 시장에서 물건을 사고파는 작은 규모의 일에 잘 어울려요. '사업하다'는 회사를 운영하는 더 큰 일이라는 느낌이 있어요. 가게가 잘될 때는 '장사가 잘돼요'라고 해요.
explain_en: 장사 suits the smaller trade of buying and selling at a shop or market. 사업하다 feels like running a bigger company. When a shop is doing well, you say 장사가 잘돼요.
